cards.title: Ukraine says U.S. early-warning channel has resumed after Oslo talks
cards.summary: AP reported that Ukraine again received early warnings of Russian missile attacks after Zelenskyy spoke with Secretary of State Marco Rubio; the wider support posture remains unsettled.
detail: The Associated Press reported that President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine was again receiving early warnings of Russian missile launches after his call with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The report followed a period in which Kyiv said attacks arrived without enough notice, including a strike that killed and wounded civilians.

The change matters because warning time is an operational part of civilian protection and air defence, even when it does not amount to a new weapons commitment. It also gives the Oslo contact a concrete, limited outcome rather than treating the meeting as a general reset in relations.

The resumption is a Ukrainian account reported by AP; it does not establish that all intelligence, satellite, or Starlink disputes are resolved. Reuters reported that Steve Witkoff was due to continue from Oslo to Moscow, while the administration described the talks as constructive.

The next test is whether the warning channel remains reliable and whether the talks produce a documented security or negotiating step. The operational improvement is reported; the durability and scope of the policy change remain uncertain.
